article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Morning Brief
article.dek: London kicks Sunday off at 9:30 a.m. ET, Huntley's -3.0 is holding, and Caleb Williams is the one name to watch on the inactives list — plus the app's three cards with real numbers.

items.headline: Sunday starts in London at 9:30 a.m. ET
paragraphs: Sunday's first kickoff isn't in the afternoon — it's at Wembley. The Texans face the Jaguars at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network, the last of three straight London games.
Jacksonville is 4-1 after beating Philadelphia 19-17 in London last week. Houston is 1-4 but finally got its first win last week. The market has Jacksonville -2.5 on DraftKings with a 42.5 total.

If you're playing anything in this game, do it before the morning gets away from you. London inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff — roughly 8:00 a.m. ET — and the app's board refreshes every morning and evening, so the card you see now is current.
items.takeaway: London goes first, so plan it first: check the app's card and inactives before 9:30 a.m. ET.

items.headline: Quarterback roundup: one game, two backups, one game-time question
paragraphs: Lamar Jackson is out for the second straight game. The Ravens ruled him out Friday with the ankle injury, so Tyler Huntley starts again at Cleveland. Huntley threw three touchdowns in last week's win at Atlanta, and the app already lists him as the expected starter — the board has fully caught up to this news.

Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely with a blood clot in his calf, so Tanner McKee starts for Philadelphia against Carolina. This morning brought one new detail: the Eagles are NOT putting Hurts on injured reserve, which keeps the door open for a return as soon as he's medically cleared. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is on injured reserve, leaving the Eagles down to their fourth-string running back.
Patrick Mahomes is cleared. He practiced fully Friday and came off the injury report, so Kansas City is at full QB strength against the Chargers.

The one live question is Caleb Williams. He's questionable with the hamstring, practiced fully all week, but Chicago is still evaluating him. Michael Penix Jr. is good to go for Atlanta after last week's rib knock. The inactives list lands about 90 minutes before each kickoff — for the 1 p.m. ET games that's about 11:30 a.m. ET — and Sunday morning's edition will carry the final word.
items.takeaway: Huntley, McKee, and Mahomes are settled facts — the app has all three. Caleb Williams is the one name to watch on the inactives list.

items.headline: Sunday weather: nothing to worry about
paragraphs: Quick check of the final kickoff-window forecasts, and there's nothing to fuss over. Foxborough is clear and sunny in the low 50s with barely any wind — the National Weather Service says sunny, high near 54, wind 3 to 5 mph. Kansas City is clear and 64 at kickoff with a light 13 mph breeze. The dome games in Atlanta, Indianapolis, and Las Vegas are unaffected by anything outside.
No rain, no wind, no cold anywhere on the slate. Weather doesn't change a single read this week.
items.takeaway: File Sunday's weather as clear and mild and move on — it doesn't move any number.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Today's three cards, with real numbers
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Bills moneyline -230 (DraftKings) vs the Raiders. This is the app's most-likely-to-win pick — about a 69% chance on the app's read. Notice what it is and isn't: at -230 you need to win about 69.7% of the time just to break even, so Hit Rate buys you win probability, not profit. The app's own tutorial says it straight: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
Balanced: Giants moneyline -104 (FanDuel) vs the Saints. The middle ground — a strong pick without paying a big price. The app's read is roughly 65% on the Giants at near even money.

Value: Falcons +1.5 (-115, FanDuel) vs the Bears. This is the app's plus-EV play — a small edge on the model side. One catch: it's priced with Caleb Williams expected to start. If he's ruled out, the math changes.
None of these are orders. They're the app's read on the board as it stands this morning.
items.takeaway: Three cards, three jobs: most likely to win, strongest middle ground, and the model's plus-EV play — pick the job you actually want done.

items.headline: Your book's number isn't the card's number? Tap Check
paragraphs: The prices above are one snapshot — DraftKings here, FanDuel there. Your book probably shows something slightly different, and 'slightly different' is where bets are won or lost.

Here's the move: open the app, tap Check, and type in the line and price your book is actually offering. The app runs your number back through the model and the evaluator and hands you a bet or no-bet verdict on YOUR price. That's a full re-evaluation, not a rubber stamp.
The board refreshes every morning and evening, so if a line moves during the day, Check is how you stay current.
items.takeaway: Never bet the card's price blind — type your book's line into Check and get the verdict on your number.

items.headline: Learn the Game: implied probability
paragraphs: Every price on the board is secretly a win-rate requirement. 'Implied probability' is just the fancy name for it: the percentage of the time a bet has to win for you to break even at that price.

A clearly-labeled hypothetical example: say a team is listed at -200 (this is made up, not a real pick). That price means you risk $2 to win $1, so it has to win 200 divided by (200 + 100) — about 66.7% of the time — to break even. At +150, the math is 100 divided by (150 + 100): the bet only needs to win 40% of the time.

Why it matters: the app's whole job is comparing its own probability against the price's implied probability. When the app's number is higher than the price demands, that's the edge — and that's exactly what the Check verdict is measuring.
items.takeaway: Implied probability turns every price into a question: does the app think this wins MORE often than the price demands? That's the edge, and that's what Check measures.

items.headline: Quiet overnight: -3.0, -3.0, -230, -115 all hold
paragraphs: Nothing moved overnight. Ravens -3.0, Panthers -3.0, Bills -230, Falcons -115 — all exactly where Friday evening left them.

The moves that matter all happened Friday: Ravens -3.5 down to -3.0 once Huntley was confirmed, Panthers -3.5 down to -3.0, Bills -218 out to -230, Falcons -110 to -115. The app's morning board has picked up every one of them, so there are no stale numbers to trip over.
If your book still shows one of the old numbers, that's a gift worth Checking — or a stale screen worth refreshing.
items.takeaway: Friday did the moving, overnight did the sleeping: the board is current on every line that matters.

items.headline: The one thing worth waiting for: Caleb Williams' status
paragraphs: There's exactly one named unknown on Sunday's board: whether Caleb Williams (questionable, hamstring) suits up for Chicago. The Falcons +1.5 card is priced with him expected to play, so if he's ruled out, the value shifts.

The inactives list for the 1 p.m. ET games lands about 90 minutes before kickoff — roughly 11:30 a.m. ET. That's a real pending event with a real time attached, and it's the only one worth waiting for today.

For everything else, the rule stands: if your book has a good number right now and Check says bet, bet now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number tomorrow, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
items.takeaway: Wait for 11:30 a.m. ET inactives only on Bears-Falcons — everywhere else, a good number now beats a hoped-for number later.

items.headline: Sunday's plan: London at 9:30, then the full slate
paragraphs: The day runs itself if you set the order now: Texans-Jaguars at 9:30 a.m. ET from London, seven games at 1 p.m. ET, three in the late afternoon window, Cowboys-Packers at 8:20 p.m. ET, and Commanders-49ers on Monday night to close the week.
Tonight's job is to lock the plan, not the bets. Decide which games you're playing and at what prices, write the plan down, and let the inactives list do its talking in the morning.
And since settlement is manual — no auto-settle anywhere in this — the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log every play you make, including the losers. Especially the losers.
items.takeaway: Plan tonight, decide in the morning: lock your games and prices now, and log every play — winners and losers — or the tracker is just a diary.

BAL expected starter Tyler Huntley (resolved), PHI Tanner McKee, CHI Caleb Williams expected.
evidence.interpretation: Board is current on Friday's news; no overnight line moves.
evidence.app_guidance: Use these prices in Check for reader's own book.

evidence.fact: Texans vs Jaguars at Wembley Stadium, London, Sunday 9:30 a.m. ET, on NFL Network (last of three straight London games). Jaguars are 4-1 after beating Philadelphia 19-17 in London last week; Texans are 1-4.
evidence.interpretation: Earliest kickoff of the weekend; first division matchup for Jacksonville.
evidence.app_guidance: Check the app's Sunday card before 9:30 a.m. ET; London inactives post ~8:00 a.m. ET.

evidence.fact: Lamar Jackson (BAL) ruled OUT vs Browns on Sunday for the second straight game (ankle). Tyler Huntley starts for Baltimore. Huntley led a 30-23 win at Atlanta in Week 5 with three TDs.
evidence.interpretation: Market has known since Friday; DK Ravens -3.0 steady overnight.
evidence.app_guidance: No action: the app already lists Huntley as expected starter and the -3.0 is priced in.

evidence.fact: Jalen Hurts (PHI) out indefinitely with a superficial blood clot in his calf; ruled out vs Panthers. Tanner McKee starts. Saturday morning, Schefter and Rapoport reported the Eagles do NOT plan to place Hurts on IR, preserving his eligibility to return once medically cleared. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is on IR; Philadelphia is down to its fourth-string running back.
evidence.interpretation: Eagles are severely shorthanded on offense; the return door stays open because Hurts avoids IR.
evidence.app_guidance: App lists McKee as expected starter; Panthers -3.0 steady overnight. Check the app Sunday morning for any change.

evidence.fact: Patrick Mahomes (KC) was a full practice participant Friday and has been removed from the Week 6 injury report. He is cleared for Sunday's home game vs the Chargers.
evidence.interpretation: No QB uncertainty in KC; the -7.5 prices a full-strength Mahomes.
evidence.app_guidance: Treat KC as at full QB strength on the app's card.

evidence.fact: Caleb Williams (CHI) is listed questionable (hamstring) for Sunday at Atlanta; he practiced fully all week but is still being evaluated. Michael Penix Jr. (ATL) was knocked out of Week 5 with a rib injury but is good to go for Week 6.
evidence.interpretation: The one genuinely live QB question on Sunday's board; the Falcons +1.5 card is priced with Williams expected.
evidence.app_guidance: Wait for the inactives list ~90 minutes before the 1 p.m. ET kickoff before pricing Bears-Falcons; re-run Check if Williams is ruled out.

evidence.fact: Patriots vs Jets at Gillette Stadium, Sunday 1 p.m. ET: clear and sunny, temperatures in the low 50s, wind chill near 49, no rain, no significant wind bursts. The National Weather Service projects sunny with a high near 54 and west wind 3 to 5 mph.
evidence.interpretation: Weather is a non-factor in Foxborough.
evidence.app_guidance: No adjustment needed on the app.

evidence.fact: Sunday outdoor games: Chargers at Chiefs (Arrowhead, 4:25 p.m. ET) — clear, 64 at kickoff, wind 13 mph gusting to 19, 0% rain. Bears at Falcons, Titans at Colts, Bills at Raiders play under closed roofs. No red-flag conditions (heavy rain, 20+ mph wind) anywhere on the Sunday slate.
evidence.interpretation: Weather is a non-factor across the Sunday slate.
evidence.app_guidance: No adjustment needed on the app.
